land.text: the British lands on the lower Severn and Cotswolds, where Wessex killed three British kings at Deorham in 577

predecessors.note: 'the kingdom was established in 577, after the Battle of Deorham' (Hwicce page). Gloucester, Cirencester and Bath were taken by the West Saxons in the same battle.

land.text: Mercia's 628 shape, which grows by 10,350 km2 over its 617 shape and includes the Hwicce

successors.note: 'After 628, the kingdom became a client or sub-kingdom of Mercia as a result of the Battle of Cirencester'; the infobox has it 'Assimilated into Mercia: 780s'. The Mercia dossier should carry the client years as a vassal_start / vassal_end with counterpart 'hwicce'.

capitals.name: Worcester
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Worcester'; 'Worcester was selected as the seat of the bishop because it was the capital of the Hwicce' (see of Worcester, 679-680). The page gives no earlier date, so 577-628 is a bridge.

keyframe_review.note: 577-586, 3,484 km2 (lat 51.71-52.52): the Worcestershire and north Gloucestershire core. The page gives no km2 figure; its described extent (Worcestershire but the north-west tip, Gloucestershire but the Forest of Dean, the south-west half of Warwickshire, the neighbourhood of Bath north of the Avon) is nearer 4,800 km2, the size of the 587 shape. The smaller 577 shape fits the page's 'West Saxon occupation of the area did not last long, and may have ended as early as 584': Gloucester, Cirencester and Bath were Wessex's after Deorham.

587-591, 4,797 km2: the shape reaches south to lat 51.38 (Bath) and matches the page's description of the whole kingdom. The year 587 is Cliopatria's; the page says the West Saxon occupation 'may have ended as early as 584'.

592-616, 4,840 km2, 43 km2 more than 587 and unexplained. In 592 'there was great slaughter at Woden's Barrow, and Ceawlin was driven out' (Ceawlin page), the end of West Saxon pressure on the Severn lands; no change of border is reported.
617-626, 4,796 km2, the same area as 592-616 to within 44 km2; unverified: page budget. The page has Hwicce undisturbed until 628.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid 627-628; from 629 the land is a client kingdom of Mercia

keyframe_review.note: 627 in Cliopatria, one year, 4,796 km2. Years: Cliopatria's row ends in 627; the Cirencester battle is 628 ('Penda took over the Severn Valley in 628 following the Battle of Cirencester') and the Hwicce page has the kingdom become a Mercian client after 628. This dossier draws the shape through 628.

region.text: Worcestershire and north Gloucestershire around Worcester

ledger.note: 577: the kingdom of the Hwicce is established after the West Saxon victory at Deorham. 'the kingdom was established in 577, after the Battle of Deorham'; the Chronicle's 577 entry has Cuthwine and Ceawlin kill three British kings and take Gloucester, Cirencester and Bath. The page describes the extent by counties, so the region is my reading.

region.text: the southern Cotswold edge toward Bath ('the neighbourhood of Bath north of the Avon')

ledger.note: 587: the Hwicce reach south toward Bath. The page says only that 'West Saxon occupation of the area did not last long, and may have ended as early as 584'; the year 587 is Cliopatria's (its Hwicce shape grows by 1,313 km2).

region.text: the whole kingdom, a client of Mercia from 628

ledger.note: 628: the Hwicce become a Mercian client. 'After 628, the kingdom became a client or sub-kingdom of Mercia as a result of the Battle of Cirencester'; sub-kings are named to 709 and the kingdom was 'Assimilated into Mercia: 780s'. Cliopatria's row ends in 627; the Penda page adds that the Hwicce sub-kingdom may have been set up by Penda, 'evidence to support this is lacking'.

wars.name: Battle of Deorham
wars.outcome: '577: Here [Cuthwine] and [Ceawlin] fought against the Britons, and they killed 3 kings, Coinmail, Condidan and Farinmail' and 'took 3 cities: Gloucester and Cirencester and Bath'; a Saxon victory at Dyrham, a few miles north of Bath. The Hwicce kingdom followed.
wars.note: The Deorham page does not mention the Hwicce; the Hwicce page ('established 577') and the Ceawlin page ('divided the Britons west of the Severn from land communication') draw the link.

wars.name: Battle of Cirencester

zones.text: Cirencester and the lower Severn valley

wars.outcome: 'Cynegils and Cwichelm fought against Penda at Cirencester and then came to an agreement'; 'Penda took over the Severn Valley in 628', and the Hwicce became a client of Mercia.
wars.note: The Hwicce page notes the Chronicle has the West Saxons fight Penda, not the Hwicce.

certainty.note: Tribal frontiers known from later diocesan and shire boundaries; no source fixes a line.

sources.title: Hwicce
sources.note: Identity, capital, Deorham 577, West Saxon occupation, 628 client status, 780s assimilation; extent by counties; no area figure.

sources.title: Battle of Deorham
sources.note: Battle of Deorham 577: the Chronicle entry, the three cities; does not mention the Hwicce.

sources.title: Ceawlin of Wessex
sources.note: Ceawlin: Dyrham, Fethanleag 584, Woden's Barrow 592, loss of the Severn lands to Penda in 628.

sources.title: Penda of Mercia
sources.note: Battle of Cirencester 628, the Severn valley and the Hwicce sub-kingdom.

notes:
Hwicce (5 Cliopatria shapes, 577-627), four pages (budget up to 5).
END 628, NOT THE 780s: the Hwicce page keeps a Hwicce sub-kingdom under Mercia until the 780s (sub-kings Eanhere, Osric, Oshere, Æthelheard and Æthelweard are named to 709). Cliopatria and this dossier end the independent state in 628. The client years 629-780 are for the Mercia dossier (vassal_start counterpart 'hwicce', vassal_end c. 780s); if it does not carry them the land is blank on the map.
587 EXPANSION: no opened page dates it; the Hwicce page says West Saxon occupation 'may have ended as early as 584'. Confidence 1.
NOT OPENED: Wessex's own page for the 584-592 retreat, a Mercia page for the 628 settlement, 'Tribal Hidage'.
The Hwicce page's Winchcombe, Wick and Lesser items were not on the page text returned.
